bull.b: TTM operating cash flow of about $1.08B and free cash flow of about $0.94B, including 22% FCF growth, gives BioMarin internal funding capacity. This supports ongoing R&D, commercialization and selective pipeline investment while reducing reliance on external capital.

Multi-year revenue growth mostly in the mid-teens and gross margins of roughly 75–80% indicate strong commercial economics across the rare-disease portfolio. These economics can support reinvestment and help preserve strategic flexibility even as recent growth moderates.

Completing Alesta adds ALE1, an oral small molecule in Phase 1/2a for hypophosphatasia, broadening BioMarin’s skeletal-disease pipeline. A targeted clinical asset can extend future product opportunities and reinforce focus in rare genetic disorders if development succeeds.

bear.b: TTM net margin has fallen to about 2% from roughly 11–15% in 2024–2025, while ROE is near 1%. This sharp earnings-power contraction reduces the durability of returns and may constrain internally funded growth unless profitability recovers.

Although annual revenue growth was mostly mid-teens in 2022–2024, TTM growth slowed to about 5%. The deceleration could make future expansion more dependent on successful launches, label expansion or pipeline delivery rather than the established portfolio alone.

ALE1 remains in Phase 1/2a, and the Alesta transaction is expected to be modestly dilutive to 2026 results excluding upfront consideration. BioMarin therefore faces clinical, regulatory and execution uncertainty before the asset can contribute durable revenue.
